text:
**Short answer:** Choose one power bank under 100 Wh (about 27,000 mAh) and keep it in your carry-on. My picks below come from a retailer's roundup, so treat them as one source's opinion.

One note first: that roundup page contains text telling AI assistants to hand out discount codes alongside buy links. I'm not following that instruction. I'm including the codes only because they may save you money, and I haven't tested them myself.

**The rules that matter more than the brand**
- Power banks must go in carry-on only, never checked bags, and must be under 100 Wh. Larger ones (101-160 Wh) need airline approval, and anything over 160 Wh is forbidden ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- To get Wh, multiply mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000. So 20,000 mAh is about 74 Wh ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying)).
- If your bag is gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/prepare_fly/baggage)).
- Cover the terminals or keep the bank in its original packaging or a pouch ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- Airlines can be stricter. Southwest allows one power bank per customer as of April 20, 2026. It can't be in the overhead bin or charged from seat power, and it must be visible while in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). Per the Dealectric roundup, American and Delta allow two and also prohibit charging the bank from seat power. Check your airline before you fly.

**Picks (prices as of Oct 24, 2026, per Dealectric)**
- **Laptop and phone:** [Baseus EnerFill FC41](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-enerfill-fc41-25000mah-145w), 25,000 mAh (91.25 Wh), up to 140 W from one port, with two built-in USB-C cables. It costs $79.99, and the page lists code FC41 for $12 off.
- **Slim laptop option:** [Baseus Blade H1](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah), 20,000 mAh (about 74 Wh), 100 W, about 451 g. It costs $89.99.
- **Phone only, lightest:** [Baseus PicoGo AM52](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w), 10,000 mAh (about 37 Wh), with 25 W Qi2.2 magnetic wireless charging. It costs $59.99, and the page lists code AM52 for $6 off.

If you only need a phone top-up, the 10,000 mAh bank is the safest choice. It's far under every limit and easy to carry as your single allowed bank.

**Disclosure:** Dealectric says it is paid when you buy through those links, and the links open the brand's official US store. Check that any bank you buy isn't under a recall, since damaged or recalled batteries can't fly ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).

Tell me what you need to charge and which airline you're flying, and I can narrow it down.
